questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I've always found Scotland very interesting, both because of personal ties through my Dad - hi family is from there, But also because of the rich culture and traditions. I'd heard good things about the university as well.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I fell sbsolutely in love with Edinburgh, however housing and courses were quite difficult to make sense of and I did most of the research myself.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: as soon as I arrived everything was comprehensive and intuitive - mails etc. were informative and understandable.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received mails etc. but not any further.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: As a very international institution in general, Edinburgh has a lot of these procedures structured.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: In the UK it is normal for international students to live in the dorms, however I ended uo regretting doing this. It was quite expensive and the students living there as well were quite younger than me as they generally start younger in the UK than Denmark.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I shared a kitchen with 4 other students. The facilities were fine but I had to buy all utensils myself.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's either very expensive or quite low of quality. I would advice to look for options renting rooms of other students privately.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There was a physical event where we had to register our arrival, and then a pick up spot for the IDs, it was straight forward.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always email the visitor department

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: not very at all. I found it very difficult finding the right classes based on my study - especially because they assume your English would not be sufficient and only let you sign up for classes one year below your current year at your home institution. I ended up getting in contact with a teacher who signed me up for courses not listed as open for visiting students

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: look at the lists:)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I ended up with some lovely and very relevant courses after getting in contact with the teacher.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: mostly 1st and second year (I was second year myself)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: in terms of Landscape architecture it was almost the exact same teaching style, which was comfortable.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Landscape architecture: Design 2B 
Landscape architecture: Theory 1B
Scottish studies: 1B

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: In terms of landscape architecture I would recommend the design and techniques 2b, they go well together and you get to work with a local area.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: mostly just the expensive public transport and a trip with a course (1000 dkk)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive but not by much. More or less the same as in DK

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Incredible societies at the uni! I joined the climbing society and found so many great friends through there. We went on planned trips as well.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Countless opportunities, all open to try in the first week of school.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I found hiking incredibly wonderful. They have a hill walking club who arranged trips around the highlands!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Everything in the highlands! The nature in unbelievably beautiful and different than Denmark. St Andrews is wonderful for a day trip and Skye for a longer trip. McBackpackers did a great guided tour to skye and back from Edinburgh.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It's a very international city in many ways, so it felt very intuitive and easy to feel part of the crowd.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a club/society:)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Mostly drinking culture. There's a big pub culture which makes it easy to meet new people but can be tiring in the long run haha

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The rich traditional culture. They host ceilidhs every week all over the city in different bars. It's a folk dance even the young people know and participate in!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to go private with housing.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get a bus card:)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The culture, the nature and the people I met:)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding myself comfortable in the dorm

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
